newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says EMU date, conditions should be met.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says EMU date, conditions should be met.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday that the planned 1999 launch date and the agreed conditions for a single European currency must be respected.

"Yes we must respect the date and conditions. That would in France's interest," Chirac said in a Bastille Day television interview, adding that failure to carry out the currency project would have "very serious consequences" for Paris.

Forced to share power with the left since his centre-right coalition was defeated in a parliamentary election on June 1, Chirac said it was his role as president to ensure international treaties were respected.

He refused to be drawn into a debate in France and Germany over whether the Maastricht Treaty rule requiring deficits to be limited to three percent of gross domestic product should be implemented right down to the last decimal point.
"That is a subject which must be handled among Europeans and certainly not in public," the president said.

Chirac said France's 1997 public deficit was running at abount 3.5 percent but the three percent goal was within reach. The new Socialist-led government has insisted the target should be interpreted as a trend rather than precise numbers, while Germany is using a strict reading of 3.0 percent.
